newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzania's new Congo refugees ready for home.
newsitem.headline: Tanzania's new Congo refugees ready for home.

text.p: The U.N. refugee agency (UNHCR) said on Wednesday the majority of an estimated 90,000 refugees who fled the former Zaire for Tanzania want to return home.
The signing of a tripartite agreement between the Democratic Republic of Congo, Tanzania and UNHCR remained the main obstacle to repatriation, Tanzanian government sources said.
"As far as the Congolese are concerned there is no resistance (to repatriation). On the contrary the majority are ready to go," said Vincent Parker, UNHCR spokesman in Tanzania.
President of the Democratic Republic of Congo Laurent Kabila and Tanzania President Benjamin Mkapa gave the green light to repatriation at the weekend, though no date has been set.
Tanzania earlier delayed the repatriation operation seeking security guarantees from Kabila's government.
"The key factor in this operation will be the availability of boats and their capacity," Parker told Reuters.

Most of the refugees -- many of whom worked as civil servants under ousted president Mobutu Sese Seko -- fled across Lake Tanganyika late last year at the start of a victorious rebellion by Kabila's troops.
